claim.value: Forcing all orders into one assumed workflow could manufacture apparent failures.
claim.scope: A conditional risk of standardization, not a finding that any observed discrepancy is artificial.

provenance.rationale: The span explicitly identifies apparent failures as a possible consequence of imposing one workflow.

signal_basis.value: Compare documentary links, timing and missing traces with route-specific predictions, looking for structured discrepancies across approval routes and handoffs; the candidate account includes permitted alternative record routes.
signal_basis.scope: Proposed observations for the sampled orders, assumed to occur for this assessment; discrepancies are relative to the modeled routes.

provenance.rationale: These spans establish alternative permitted routes, comparison with route predictions, the discrepancy signal and its proposed-observation status.
The bounded possibility claim is supported without an unresolved empirical relation.

rationale: A permitted route can differ from an imposed workflow. Comparing its records against that workflow can therefore generate a mismatch that appears to be a process failure. This licenses the stated possibility, without establishing that any particular discrepancy is artificial.
uncertainty: Whether this risk materialized for any sampled order remains undetermined.
